feedback.problem: If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=7$ and $f(7)=13,$ then what is ${lim}_{x\to {7}^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-f(x))?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We're told that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=7.$ According to the definition of continuity, this means that ${lim}_{x\to 7}f(x)$ exists and

$$
{lim}_{x\to {7}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to 7}f(x)=f(7)=13.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {7}^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-f(x)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{2}-13) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(36) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡6.\end{aligned}
$$
